full_judgment:
2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 58 of 1991 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj impleading the opposite parties as defendants praying for a decree declaring their title to the suit land and for further decree that the suit land was not vested and non-resident property. The suit land measuring 4.40 acres of land of Mouza Rajdia under police station Serajdikhan, District Munshiganj as described in the 'ka' schedule to the plaint was recorded in the name of Lal Mohan Mukhepadhya. Kunju Mohan Mukhopadhy. Upendra Mohan Mukhopadhy, Kalipada Horipada Mukhopadhy, Binod Ranjan Mukhopadhy and Surendra Mohan Mukhopadhy in the CS Khatian No. 594 and the names of Shasanka Mohan Mukhopadhya, brother of Lal Mohan and Junja Mohan Mukhopadhya were inadvertently not recorded and the land measuring 1.30 acres of Mouja Rajdia as described in 'kha' schedule to the plaint was recorded in the names of Sasanka Mohan Mukhopadhya and Kunju Mohan Mukhopadhya in equal shares in the CS Khatian No. 176. 

 4. Thereafter Shasanka Mohan died leaving his son Birendra Mohan as only heir and Kunju Mohan died leaving Nirmal Mukhopadhya as only heir to their respective lands SA Khatian in respect of the suit land was published in the names of Girendra Mohan and Kunju Mohan Mukhopadhya. 

 5. While Nirmal Mukhopadhya was owning and possessing his inherited land, he sold 65 acres of land of 'kha' schedule along with some land of another khatian of same Mouja to these plaintiff petitioners by kabala deed No. 10467 executed on 29-4-1975 and registered on 4-5-1975 in the office of Sadar Sub-Registrar Dhaka and that Birendra Mohan Mukhopadhya while owning and possessing his inherited land sold 4.40 acres of land from 'ka' schedule land and 0.6 acres from 'kha' schedule land along with some land of another khatian of same mouza to those plaintiff petitioners by kabala deed No. 10468 and 10469 executed on 29-4-1975 and registered on 8-5-1975, in the office of Sadar Sub-Registrar, Dhaka and possession of the land was handed over to the plaintiff-petitioners. The plaintiff petitioners thereafter mutated their names in the office of Assistant Commissioner, (Land) Serajdikhan and have been paying rents. They by constructing huts in some parts and cultivating and growing crops in other parts have been possessing their purchased land for over 12 years, without any interruption and to the knowledge of all and thus the plaintiff-petitioners have acquired good title to the suit land adversely to all. 

 7. The opposite party No. 1 as defendant No. 3 contested the suit by filing written statement. The case of the opposite party No. 1, in short, is that the land described in 'ka' schedule land belonged to Lal Mohan, Kunju Mohan, Upendra Mohan, Kalipada, Haripad, and Binod Ranjan and Surendra. The SA Khatian of this land was wrongly recorded in the name of Birendra who has no manner of right, title and, possession therein. Birendra was the Principal of Haraganga College. Munshigonj and he migrated to India in 1947 leaving his job and he died there. The further defence case in that Shashanka was the owner of plot No. 310 under 'kha' schedule land by way of amicable settlement but as the owner of this land left for India in 1987 so the suit land was enlisted as vested property and was given lease to Md Ali and Ismail Chokder, the father of plaintiff Nos. 2 to 4. As they removed the valuable things and trees so they were evicted therefrom. The name of Birendra was not included in the voter list and they did neither reside at Brajdia nor they pay tax of Union Parishad. The land of 'Kha' Schedule was given lease in VP case No. 557 of 1968 to Sayed Ali Ashraf, Hazrat Ali and Ismail. The plaintiff-petitioners created forged documents on 29-4-1975 in order to grab the suit land 0.34 decimals of land under 'kha' schedule was given in lease to Motiur Rahman and others and the sale deeds dated 29-4-1975 in the name of plaintiff petitioners are forged which were created by Islam personification. It is further stated in the written statement that Birendra was not a citizen of Bangladesh and he was shown as an Indian national. Birendra or his father Shoshanka did never possess the land of 'ka' schedule land. 

 16. It appears from plaint and the deposition of witnesses of plaintiffs, that 'ka' schedule land comprised of 4.40 acres appertaining to plot Nos. 396, 436, 417 and 414 of CS Khatian No. 594 and of SA Khatian No. 574 and 'kha' schedule land comprised of 1.30 acres appertaining to plot No. 410 of CS Khatian No. 176 and SA Khatian No. 100. It further appears from evidence on record that 'ka' schedule land belonged to Lal Mohan Konju Mohon, Upendra Mohan, Kalipada, Haripada, Binod Ranjan and Surendra and lcha' schedule land belonged to Shashanka and Kanuja Mohan. 

 17. Learned Subordinate judge by the judgment dated 30-11-1993 held that Nirmal and Birendra acquired the 'ka' and 'kha' schedule land. by family arrangement" and having title and possession therein they sold the suit land to the plaintiff petitioners by three kabala deeds marked exhibit No. 1/1, 2/2 and 3/3, It further appears from the evidence on record that the plaintiff petitioners have been possessing the suit land by creating huts in one portion and cultivating crops in the other portion. The plaintiff-petitioners also mutated their names and paid rents to the Government Mutation, Khatians are marked exhibit 3 to 3(7a) and thereat receipts are marked exhibit 4 to 4 (Gha). The learned Assistant Additional District Judge did not make any comment on these points. Excepting about the jurisdiction of Sub-Registrar, Sadar, Dhaka to execute and register the deeds marked exhibit 1, 2 and 3 in his impugned judgment dated 2-11-1998. Trial Court and lower appellate Court are the courts effects. The silence of the learned Additional District Judge in these points indirectly indicates the acceptance of the finding of the trial Court. We having exercised revisional jurisdiction do not like to go deep into these points. Moreover, it further appears from the evidence on record that findings of the trial Court are well reasoned which should not be interfered. 

 23. PW 2 Ibrahim Howlader deposed that suit land is near his house; that Birendra and Nirmal were the owners of the suit land by amicable partition, petitioner that Birendra was the son of Sasanta and Nirmal was the son of Kanjo; that he saw Birend and Nirmal to possess the suit land; that he saw Birendra and Nirmal 4/5 years after the liberation of Bangladesh; that Birendra and Nirmal sold the suit land to the plaintiff-petitioners who was in possession of the same. Their names were record in CS records of right and CS Khatian is marked exhibit I(ga). Sasanko possessed the land of 'ka' schedule on behalf of his brothers. Birendra Mohan Mukhopadhya is the only son of Sasanko. 'Ka' schedule land was recorded in the name of Birendra in SA Khatian marked exhibit I (ka), 'kha' schedule land was recorded in the name of Sasanko Mohan Mukhopadhay and Kunju Mohon Moukhopadhay in equal share in SA Khatian No 176 which is marked exhibit No.1. Kunjo died leaving only son Nirmal, Birendra and Nirmal acquired the 'ka' and 'kha' schedule land by family arrangement and having title and possession therein sold the same on 29-4-1975, to the plaintiffs and they have been possessing the suit land creating huts and living therein, catching fishes from the pond and growing crops in the nal-land.
